 Purpose of the Commission: The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate
 for equity, access, diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural
 competency, positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, OCTOBER 25, 2022
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:33 p.m.
on Tuesday, October 25, 2022, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Herrera.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Jacqueline Borja, Michelle Brenhaug, Susan Fitzsimmons, Viki Goto
  Jorge Herrera and Chasity Jennings-Nuñez

Commissioners Absent:  Riaz (Rick) Khan

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez hearing no objections, the Agenda Order was approved.

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 25, 2022
   Andrew Didia would like to see equal representation on the HEAR Commission. He believes
  there should be more male commissioners.

  3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  Vice Chair Goto requested an addition to the minutes.

  A motion was made by Commissioner Brenhaug and seconded by Commissioner
  Fitzsimmons to approve the updated minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular
  Meeting for September 27, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 6-0-0-1 as follows:
  Ayes: Borja, Brenhaug, Fitzsimmons, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez
  Nays: None
  Abstain: None
  Absent: Khan

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. GUEST SPEAKER – FOOTHILL FAMILY
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez introduced the guest speakers, Erin Copeland and Melissa
  Alaniz from Foothill Family. They provided information on new programs and
  services such as relative support services, elder abuse treatment and the parents
  invested in relationship success programs.

  The Commission thanked the speakers and asked about their programs. They
  inquired about individualized coaching and the kinship program. The
  Commission requested that informational flyers be included in lunch distribution
  for seniors. They also asked if there was an uptick in cases and if so, what the
  numbers and causes were. Commissioners would like to partner with Foothill
  Family for their new year workplan. They also want to see scam prevention
  seminars provided in San Gabriel.

  B. GUEST SPEAKER – ASIAN YOUTH CENTER
  Vice-Chair Goto introduced Heidi Lau from the Asian Youth Center. Ms. Lau shared
  information regarding their agency’s new Stop Hate Steering Committee.

  The Commission thanked the speaker for all they do in the community. The
  Commission suggested that seminars be offered in other languages and expressed
  it would be important to broaden their reach to more groups, such as Latinx and
  LGBT+. Commissioners asked how the public can find information for AYC’S
  upcoming events and inquired about the best way to report a hate crime.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 25, 2022
   Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided the update.

  The Commission discussed the results of the Engagement Survey. The Commission
  thanked Commissioner Borja and Vice Chair Goto for developing this survey. The
  Commission has one more incentive item to distribute. Staff were directed to pull
  the name at random and the winner will be announced at the next meeting. They
  will look into different, more engaging ways of selecting a winner for future
  drawings.

  For Native American Heritage month, the Commission announced a video will be
  shown in its entirety at the November meeting.

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Commissioner Brenhaug will be at the Family Fun Festival with McKinley
  Elementary School PTA.

  Commissioner Fitzsimmons shared it is Pink Patch Month and encouraged people
  to get mammograms. She also wanted to recognize Hispanic Heritage Month.
  Commissioner Fitzsimmons commended the Community Engagement Team for
  assisting a resident in need. She encouraged everyone to go out and vote since
  elections are approaching.

  Vice Chair Goto attended the community benefit advisory quarterly meeting with
  the City of Hope. She will be sharing findings on mental health once the report is
  finalized and published. She shared the Health Consortium of the greater San
  Gabriel will host a virtual conference discussing behavioral health on December 8th.
  Vice Chair Goto recommended an L.A. Times & Pen America virtual event, Reading
  Between the Lines, on November 3rd, it will be addressing race, equity, cultural
  diversity, and publishing today. She also wanted to highlight Anna May Wong
  becoming the first Asian American to be featured on U.S currency.

  Commissioner Herrera invited the community to watch Grammy award winning
  mariachi, Los Camperos at the Mission Playhouse on November 5th.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez invited the community to participate in the city’s Dia de los
  Muertos Celebration. She announced that October also recognizes Filipino
  American and Italian American cultural heritages as well as Domestic Violence
  Awareness Month and Breast Cancer Wellness Month. She also advised there could

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  OCTOBER 25, 2022
   be a peak in COVID cases this winter and suggested getting your boosters and
  taking the proper precautions. She reminded the public about upcoming elections.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens provided staff comments.

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:10 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is scheduled in person for Tuesday, November 22, 2022 at 6:30 p.m.
